content.text:
**Choose Sentry**, unless you're mostly a mobile team (then consider Bugsnag). I wrote this from memory, so check current pricing on each vendor's page before you commit. All three change their tiers often.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core strength** | Errors plus tracing, performance and session replay in one product | Error grouping and deploy tracking, with a simple workflow | Mobile stability, with release health and stability scores |
| **SDK coverage** | The broadest: web, backend, mobile, game engines | Broad, but strongest on backend and web | Broad, with the best mobile depth (iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter) |
| **Pricing model** | Based on event volume. Team plans include unlimited users, starting around $26/mo | Based on event volume. Unlimited seats, with entry plans around $14–$70/mo | Based on seats and event volume, so it usually costs the most for a 10-person team |
| **Free tier** | Yes, but limited to 1 user | Yes, about 5k events/mo | Yes, but very limited |
| **Self-hosting** | Yes (source-available), though it's heavy to run | No | No |
| **Integrations** | Excellent: GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, PagerDuty | Good | Good, with Jira and Slack |
| **Main downside** | Event quotas can surprise you in a spike, so you need rate limits and sampling | Fewer features beyond errors, and a smaller ecosystem | Pricier, and it has less to offer outside mobile |

**Why Sentry for 10 people**
- **Cost:** Per-seat pricing doesn't hurt you, and the Team plan covers a small team's volume.
- **One tool, fewer vendors:** You get errors, performance traces and session replay together. That lets you skip a separate APM tool early on.
- **Ecosystem:** It has the most community support, docs and framework integrations, so setup is quick and hiring is easier.
- **Exit option:** You can self-host if cost or data residency becomes a problem.

**When to pick something else**
- **Bugsnag:** Your product is mainly a mobile app and you care about crash-free sessions as a release metric.
- **Rollbar:** You only want error tracking, you like its grouping and deploy-tracking workflow, and you want predictable costs.

**To avoid surprise bills with Sentry:** set per-project rate limits, turn on spike protection, and filter out noisy errors such as browser extensions and bot traffic. Start on the free or Team plan, and run a 2-week trial on your highest-traffic service to see your real event volume before committing.

If you tell me your stack (web, mobile, backend languages) and your rough monthly traffic, I can tighten this up. I can also look up current pricing.
